reviews.review:
I sought a game with a compelling gameplay loop that could be played in short intervals with meaningful progress and strong cooperative elements.

I have found rock and stone.

Honostly, out of every 4 player coop game ive played, this one stands out like a beacon.

Art style, mechanics, exploration, guns bugs bombs and bullets. This one just feels right when playing with people. Other reviews can praise those more than i will, but theres one thing that i adore about the game, and the community about this game.

TEAMWORK!!!

I absolutely adore the teamwork in this game, especially if you and your teammates (i usually play with randoms) have a good idea with how objectives and mechanics work (which is pretty easy to work out). Because there always seems to be an unspoken rule of "if it broke, we're gonna fix it" and not "if it broke, i'll leave that to them". 

And even more so with heavy objects, like gold chucks, crystals, eggs and Doretta. Because you'll notice that when you're carrying heavy objects, your teammates with look at you, while standing still, as a silent "im open, throw it". I adore it everytime i see it.

One other thing are the classes. 9 times out of 10, no matter what squad i join, with will always choose to  each be a seperate class, no dupe classes. Now obviously this is a rule that can be imposed, but even then, most of the time, its not imposed, people just choose to be whatever is not there. This makes it easy for ANY situation.

Gunner: Ziplines that allow everyone to travel across any cavern, and the bubble shield that makes reviving MUCH safer.

Scout: Their flare gun that lights up the caves like ya got night vision, and the grappling hook that allows them to quickly get to objectives, downed teammates and out of reach mineral deposits.

Engineer: That platform gun may seem boring, but that thing makes SO MANY things easy to deal with. Platform under a high up mineral deposit for your scout to stand on, platform a staircase on the side of ledges, platform across gaps, platform a hole shut so bugs cant get through, a landing pad for high drops (if you have the perk). The possibilities are impressive with this one tool.

Driller: aah, my main. Listen, we drillers are a simple type. Drilling holes for a simple path through, up, and down, is like dopamine to us. If we have an excuse for digging a whole, WE'RE GONNA DO IT. And the one thing you'll almost always see a driller do, is when the drop pod comes down for the pick up, us drillers will BEELINE IT to the drop pod. It don't matter, we got fuel left, we're gonna use it to get our boys back home.

Glad i found this game.

Deep Rock Galactic is easily a top 3 game of all time. The gameplay loop is amazing and avoids being repetitive. There has not been a moment on this game I was not having a good time. Rock and Stone forever.

Turns out you can make an online game without predatory monetization.

The gatha-like upgrades, tons of cosmetics, season passes - everything for making turing it into nightmare is there. But nobody pulled the trigger. Everything is free. You only need to buy the game once. waow.

And somehow community is not toxic. Normally I'm not a fan of online games unless I'm playing with my friends only. Here, playing with randoms won't make you reconsider your life decision. Just hit "V" to "rock and stone" from time to time and you will be good. Yelling "rock and stone" is the core point of experience + it is crucial for your survival.

About the game itself - the gunplay is good. The each class plays totally different, but each is fun. There is only PvE, so no need to use meta(TM) builds. Monsters go kaboom, so it is good for me.

And ignore the reviews saying that the game is no longer updated. The next big update comes in January - new season, new biome, and new mission type.
